intended_object: The functor from snake-lemma input diagrams in an abelian category to short complexes. It sends a snake diagram S to the part ker v₂ → ker v₃ →δ coker v₁ of the snake sequence (in the file's notation, `S.L₀.X₂ ⟶ S.L₀.X₃ ⟶ S.L₃.X₁`, where the second map is the connecting morphism δ). This reading comes from the docstring and from the surrounding snake-lemma API.
explanation: On objects, the functor gives `S.L₁'`, which is `ShortComplex.mk S.L₀.g S.δ _`: the short complex X₂ → X₃ →δ L₃.X₁ in the snake sequence. A morphism f of snake inputs goes to the morphism of short complexes with components f.f₀.τ₂, f.f₀.τ₃ and f.f₃.τ₁. These components match the objects involved. The first square commutes because the morphism f₀ of short complexes commutes, and the second because δ is natural (`naturality_δ`). So this is the usual functoriality of this piece of the snake exact sequence. Abelian categories are the standard setting for the snake lemma, so the definition is not too narrow. It belongs to the general snake-lemma development and does not duplicate another Mathlib declaration.
